name: 3D Viewer Online
author: 3dvieweronline

sections.description:
Show your products in 3D on your WordPress website or WooCommerce store. The 3DVieweronline plugin embeds models hosted on 3DVieweronline, so customers can explore products alongside descriptions, specifications, downloads and purchasing information.

Use your existing supported CAD and 3D files to present industrial components, equipment and other products. Visitors can inspect published models in a compatible browser without installing specialist desktop viewing software.

Try the plugin live

Explore a ready-made WooCommerce product with the plugin installed. Try the 3D viewer, edit the model URL and change the plugin settings.

Launch the interactive demo

The demo runs in your browser and may take a moment to start. Changes are temporary and are lost when you reload or close it.

See the 3D product viewer in action

Watch how an interactive 3D model fits into a product page alongside product information.

Built for 3d product catalogues

3DVieweronline is a hosted 3D viewing service for businesses presenting products online. Use it to bring interactive CAD and 3D models into product pages, technical catalogues and customer communications.

More than 7 million models uploaded. Trusted by over 90,000 businesses. Organisations featured on our website include Princeton University Library, Craftcloud, Laude, Osculati, Power Belt and Zemic.

Make each model fit your website

Customise each model’s viewer layout in your 3DVieweronline account. Adjust colours, backgrounds and available toolbar functions to blend the embedded viewer into your website and keep the controls focused on what your customers need. Available options depend on your plan.

Try it free for two weeks

Register for a free 14-day Business Plan trial, with no commitment and no payment card required. Test your own models, customise the viewer and try embedding it in your website.

Need more time? Contact us through our website to request a trial extension.

Let customers explore your products

  • Rotate and zoom to inspect products from different angles.
  • Help customers understand shapes, connections and component details.
  • Add interactive models to WordPress pages, posts and WooCommerce product pages.
  • Use the hosted viewer’s available measurement tools to examine dimensions.
  • Adapt the viewer’s presentation to your website through your 3DVieweronline account, subject to your plan and configuration.

WordPress and WooCommerce integration

  • Add a model URL using the 3DVo Embed — Pages & Posts block.
  • Embed a model using the [3Dvo-model] shortcode.
  • Associate a hosted model URL with a WooCommerce product.
  • Display product models in a product tab or open them from a 3D icon using the plugin’s classic WooCommerce placements.
  • Use the 3DVo Embed — Product Template block in product templates to display the model associated with the current product.
  • Set the viewer’s width and height to suit your page layout.

WooCommerce is optional for pages, posts and shortcodes. Product features require WooCommerce. Product placement depends on your theme and templates.

Use your existing CAD and 3D files

The hosted service supports formats including STEP, IGES, STL, OBJ, GLTF, 3MF and DWG. Capabilities and file requirements vary by format. Check the current information on the 3D product viewer page before preparing your models.

Upload and manage files in your 3DVieweronline account, then add their viewer URLs to WordPress. Model storage and processing are provided by the hosted service; this plugin embeds the resulting viewer.

A model library independent of your website

Keep your hosted models in one 3DVieweronline account and connect them to the relevant product pages. Supported plans offer multiple-file uploads for preparing a catalogue. Storage and upload limits depend on your account.

If you change website platforms, your hosted models remain in your 3DVieweronline account. You will just need to add their viewer URLs or embed codes to the new website.

External service and account requirements

This plugin connects your website to the external 3DVieweronline service. You need a 3DVieweronline account and a plan that includes website embedding. The plugin is free to install; hosted embedding requires an eligible paid plan or trial.

Models are uploaded to 3DVieweronline through your account. When a page displays an embedded model, the visitor’s browser connects to 3DVieweronline to load the viewer and model content.

Please review the service information before use:

  • Plans
  • Terms and conditions
  • Privacy policy
  • Help
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate 3D Viewer Online from Plugins > Add Plugin, or upload the plugin ZIP.
  2. Create or sign in to your 3DVieweronline account and upload a supported product model.
  3. Ensure your account includes website embedding and that the model’s access settings permit the intended audience to view it.
  4. Copy the model’s viewer URL.
  5. For a page or post, add the 3DVo Embed — Pages & Posts block and paste the URL.
  6. For a WooCommerce product, enter the URL in its 3D Viewer Online fields. Choose your display options in the 3D Viewer Online admin menu.

Minimum requirements: WordPress 6.3 and PHP 7.4. WooCommerce is required only for product integration.

Try an example model

Want to test the plugin before uploading your own model? Copy this public demonstration URL:

https://www.3dvieweronline.com/viewer/members/Id9bf31c7ff062936a96d3c8bd1f8f2ff3/aGuerhOXgVrJygl

For a page or post, paste it into the 3DVo Embed — Pages & Posts block.

For a WooCommerce product, paste it into the product’s 3D Viewer Online model URL field, save the product and view its page.

This URL displays our demonstration model. To publish your own products, upload your models to your 3DVieweronline account.
sections.faq:
Is the plugin free?

The plugin is free to install. Website embedding uses the hosted 3DVieweronline service and requires an eligible paid plan or trial. Check the plans page for current terms.

Do I need WooCommerce?

No. You can embed models in WordPress pages and posts without WooCommerce. WooCommerce is required for product-specific features.

How do I use the shortcode?

Add a Shortcode block and enter the following, replacing YOUR_MODEL_URL with your model’s viewer URL:

[3Dvo-model url=”YOUR_MODEL_URL” width=”100%” height=”500px”]

Which block should I use?

For a WordPress page or post:

Add “3DVo Embed — Pages & Posts” and paste your model’s viewer URL into the block.

For a WooCommerce product using the plugin’s tab or popup:

You do not need a block. Enter the model URL in the product’s “3D Viewer Online” fields and choose the display options in the plugin settings.

For a WooCommerce product template edited with blocks:

First save a model URL in each product’s “3D Viewer Online” fields. Then open Appearance > Editor > Templates > Single Product and add “3DVo Embed — Product Template” where you want the viewer.

This block reads the URL from the product being viewed. It has no URL field of its own. The editor displays a placeholder; the interactive model appears on the published product page. Products without a saved model URL display no viewer.

Editing the Single Product template requires a compatible block theme. If your theme does not offer this editor, use the plugin’s product tab or popup settings instead.

How do I customise the viewer?

Set the embedded viewer’s dimensions in the block, shortcode or plugin settings. Edit each model’s viewer layout in your 3DVieweronline account, including colours, backgrounds and available toolbar functions, to integrate it with your website. Options depend on your plan.

Does the plugin upload or convert CAD files?

Upload and process models through your 3DVieweronline account. This plugin displays hosted models using their viewer URLs; it does not add file conversion or bulk-upload tools to WordPress.

Can I use a large product catalogue?

Yes, the number and size of models you can host depend on your account’s storage and upload limits.

Will customers need specialist software?

No, published models open in a compatible web browser. Performance and available interactions depend on the device, browser and model complexity.
